source_row.rationale: CT scan is often the initial imaging choice for suspected acute intracranial hemorrhage because it is generally faster to obtain and highly sensitive for detecting acute blood, making it well-suited for emergent evaluation, while MRI (though providing superior detail for many other neurological conditions) is typically slower and less immediately available in emergent situations.
source_row.source_detail: Rationale for CT as Initial Emergent Imaging
source_row.source_name: AAN — CT vs. MRI Selection in Acute Neurological Evaluation
